title: Honest dealing
hook: no cheating, no hiding faults in goods (Muslim)
tomorrow: when exactly do you owe someone their pay?

segments.voice: Yesterday, work as worship: a king at a workbench, measuring every link. Honest hands. Today, the other end of the job: selling.

Online listings have a language of their own. Gently used. Minor wear. Works great. Now a market stall, in Sahih Muslim. The Prophet ﷺ passes a heap of grain and pushes his hand into it. His fingers come out wet. Rain fell on it, the seller says. That's true. He didn't lie, and the rain wasn't his fault. And still the Prophet calls it cheating. Why?
screen: `GENTLY USED. WORKS GREAT.` → `A HAND IN THE GRAIN.` → `TRUE, AND STILL CHEATING?`

segments.voice: Here's what he said: why didn't you put the wet part on top, so people could see it? Whoever cheats is not of me. The word he uses is ghashsha, to cheat. And the seller's wrong wasn't the rain. It was the arrangement: dry grain on top, the flaw underneath. He never said a false word. He let the heap say it for him. That's the puzzle solved. Cheating here isn't only lying. It's hiding. A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari says it from the other side: if buyer and seller tell the truth and make things clear, their deal is blessed; if they hide things and lie, the blessing of the deal is wiped out. Notice the pair. Tell the truth, and make things clear. Two duties, not one, and you can keep the first and still fail the second. So, the modern stall. Minor wear, when the zipper's broken. The photo taken from the good side. The noise in the car nobody asked about. None of it is quite a lie. All of it is wet grain at the bottom. One to tell a friend: the Prophet checked the grain with his own hand.
screen: `WHY NOT ON TOP?` · `NOT ONLY LYING: HIDING.` · `TRUTH, AND CLARITY.` · `THE MODERN STALL.` · then, large: `NOTHING HIDDEN.`

segments.voice: Choose one thing you own that you might sell or lend someday. On paper, write its honest listing in two lines, the flaw first. Read it back once, and sit with it for the rest of the time.
screen: `ONE THING YOU OWN.` · `TWO LINES, FLAW FIRST.`

segments.voice: Honest dealing: buying and selling with the truth told and the flaw in plain sight. Not only no lies; nothing hidden.
For the road: nothing hidden, the wet grain on top where anyone can see it. That's two of ten.

screen: `DAY 1703 COUNTS.` → `WORK AND MONEY · 2 OF 10.` → `TOMORROW: WHEN EXACTLY DO YOU OWE SOMEONE THEIR PAY?`

howItsDone: Muslim traders are taught to point out defects in goods before a sale; a hidden fault can give the buyer the right to undo the deal, and honest disclosure is treated as part of a blessed trade.

match.prompt: the stall and the lesson — tap the pairs.

myth: in the hadith, the grain seller told a lie
he said rain fell on it, which was true. the cheat was hiding the wet part underneath.
a hadith says hiding a flaw wipes out a deal's blessing
if they tell the truth and make things clear, the deal is blessed; if they hide and lie, its blessing is wiped out.

fork.setup: you're selling your bike online. the gears slip in the rain; on a dry test ride nobody would notice. what does the wet grain say?
options: list it as is; the test ride is the buyer's chance to check.
put the slipping gears in the listing, right up top.
drop the price a little and say nothing; the discount covers it.
fork.reveal: the grain seller didn't lie either. the Prophet asked why the wet part wasn't on top, so people could see it.

original.note: Arabic: cheating, deceit. 'whoever cheats (ghashsha) is not of me.'

trapdoor: what you thought: honest dealing means don't lie.
what it means: it also means don't hide: the flaw goes on top, where people can see it.
what a scholar hears: Muslim 102, the wet heap, 'whoever cheats is not of me'; Bukhari 2079, truth and clarity bless a sale, hiding and lying wipe out its blessing.
guess: trading with nothing about the goods hidden
never haggling over the price of anything
selling only to people of your own faith

chat.says: dad wants the old espresso machine sold online. it leaks a little. do i say so if nobody asks?
options: Yes, put it in the listing. Hiding the flaw is the cheat, even without a lie.
Only if the buyer asks. Silence isn't a lie, so you're in the clear.
Mention it after the sale. That way it's honest and it's still sold.
chat.meaning: The grain seller told no lie, yet the Prophet called hiding the wet part cheating. Truth and clarity both: the flaw goes on top.

Sahih Muslim.meaning: a major collection of the Prophet's sayings, by Imam Muslim

Sahih al-Bukhari.meaning: a major collection of reports of the Prophet's words and deeds
